messages:
natalie: Heads up — StratusHealth POC failing TLS to our private endpoint. App logs show `tls: handshake failure`. Customer says it works from their laptop but not from their VPC. Can infra team triage? :eyes:

alex: Ok. Two likely culprits: private DNS / routing or egress firewall doing TLS inspection and breaking OCSP stapling. Can you paste the exact app error + a quick `dig`/`curl` from their app host?

natalie: Here are the snippets customer pasted:
```
2025-10-18T14:02:12Z error: rpc failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2025-10-18T14:02:12Z debug: OCSP stapling missing, responder timeout
```
They also ran a `curl` and got: `curl: (35) SSL connect error`.

jordan: Thanks — can they run `openssl s_client -connect private-api.stratus.internal:443 -servername private-api.stratus.internal -status` from the app host (or a bastion in the same subnet) and paste output? That shows OCSP status.

natalie: They ran it and returned: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
TLS server name: private-api.stratus.internal
OCSP response: no response sent
verify return:1
139736...: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
---
read:errno=104
```
Customer note: "We are behind a corporate firewall appliance doing TLS inspection."

alex: That lines up. Many inspection proxies intercept TLS, re-sign certs, and don't honor stapled OCSP or block outbound connections to OCSP responders (usually over HTTP/80). If the proxy can't reach the OCSP responder, some clients fail the handshake.

maria: Quick troubleshooting checklist: 1) Confirm private DNS resolves to private IP (split-horizon). 2) Verify route table -> NAT or IGW for egress to public OCSP host. 3) Check firewall appliance allows outbound TCP 80 to OCSP responder and/or allow passthrough for that FQDN. 4) Test with SNI passthrough or disable inspection for this host.

natalie: dig output from their app host: `dig +short private-api.stratus.internal` -> `10.2.3.4` (private IP). So DNS is fine.

jordan: Good. Next: from the same host, run `curl -v --resolve "private-api.stratus.internal:443:10.2.3.4" https://private-api.stratus.internal/` and `tcpdump -n -s0 -A port 80 or port 443` while attempting the curl. We want to see if outbound to ocsp.* is attempted and whether it's failing.

natalie: They ran tcpdump and saw connections to the firewall but no outbound to ocsp.globalsign.com — looks like the appliance is terminating and not forwarding OCSP or blocking egress.

alex: Two mitigations: A) Add firewall rule to allow outbound TCP 80/443 to known OCSP/CRL responder hostnames for the issuing CAs OR B) configure the appliance to bypass MITM for `private-api.stratus.internal` (SNI passthrough). Option A is usually faster for enterprise approval.

maria: Customer ops said they can add an egress allowlist. Suggested rule: `ALLOW tcp 80,443 to ocsp.globalsign.com, ocsp.digicert.com, crl3.digicert.com` (they should verify exact responder hosts from the cert chain). Also note some CAs use HTTP on port 80 for OCSP.

jordan: Quick test commands for them after rule change: 
```
# verify OCSP reachable
curl -v http://ocsp.globalsign.com/
# verify TLS handshake and stapling
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.4:443 -servername private-api.stratus.internal -status
```

natalie: Customer ops applied the allowlist and re-ran `openssl s_client`. New output: `OCSP Response: successful (0x0)`, handshake completes. App logs show no more x509 errors.

alex: Awesome. Action items: 1) Sales to confirm customer will keep the allowlist after POC (they agreed). 2) SRE/solutions to document the required egress endpoints for enterprise docs and the recommended firewall policy (bypass MITM or whitelist OCSP/CRL hostnames). 3) Add note to the POC ticket about private DNS + MITM pitfalls.

maria: I'll update the POC runbook and send the list of OCSP hostnames we saw in the cert chain.

infrabot: POC-4627 updated: "StratusHealth — Private endpoint TLS handshake blocked by corporate TLS inspection; mitigation: egress allowlist for OCSP/CRL or MITM bypass" (link: https://go.redwood/POC-4627)

natalie: Customer confirmed tests passed and they're moving to validation phase. Thanks team :tada:
